company_name: Power Grid Corporation of India Limited

inputs.share_count_basis: 9,300.60m shares of Rs10 face value; basic = diluted (no options, convertibles or share-based payment). Held flat: growth capex is funded from retained earnings and debt, no equity raise assumed.
inputs.sbc_source: No share-based payment: government CPSE, no equity awards. SBC rows kept explicit at 0%; house and street bases coincide.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z NSE regular close (last session before the valuation date)
inputs.net_debt_note: Consolidated balance sheet at 30 Sep 2026 (Q2 FY2027 results, Rs crore x10): borrowings 1,26,218.37 non-current + 24,988.63 current = 1,51,207.00 crore; cash and equivalents 2,520.91 + other bank balances 3,648.23 = 6,169.14 crore. Rs1,809 crore of the cash sits in designated project accounts and is still counted. Lease liabilities (Rs62 crore) are immaterial and excluded.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR. Risk-free ~6.5-6.6% (India 10Y G-sec, house reference also used on HDB/IBN), equity risk premium ~6.75-7%, beta 0.7 for a regulated transmission monopoly -> cost of equity ~11.3-11.5%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~7.4% (AAA domestic), 6.1% after the 17.5% MAT cash rate. Weights 50/50, the midpoint between market-value weights at the current price (62/38 equity/debt, which gives 9.4%) and the 30/70 regulatory project structure (7.7%) -> 8.5%. One WACC for all three scenarios; risk is carried in the flows and the weights, not the rate. The choice of weights is the single most consequential judgment in this model. With the 20x terminal cap binding, lowering WACC alone does not recover the current price in the base case (the sensitivity grid tops out below it at 6.5%); the price needs both a rate near the 7.5-7.7% regulatory-structure WACC and an uncapped Gordon terminal value, or bull-case project economics.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment A by default: leases are immaterial (Rs62 crore liabilities, Rs11 crore annual payment), neither deducted from flows nor added to net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: No non-controlling interest on the consolidated balance sheet; nothing to deduct.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company, non-US' plus the adaptations file). A regulated transmission utility is not a REIT, bank or holdco: its EBITDA, capex and net debt mean what the engine assumes, and reported FCF being near zero in a capex supercycle is the SKILL's named trap, not a reason to change model. The care is in the build, not the route: (1) revenue is not extrapolated but built from capitalisation -- incremental revenue = first-year tariff yield on assets capitalised (half-year lag) less the tariff decay on the legacy cost-plus RAB as loans amortise and assets pass year 12 of the CERC depreciation schedule; (2) capex is carried at the guided Rs37,000-40,000 crore and the Rs2.20 lakh crore order book through FY2032, then glides to the level consistent with terminal growth, so the terminal year capitalises a steady state rather than a supercycle year; (3) 10-year horizon because FCF is negative through FY2030 and only matures after the order book is executed. EBITDA = revenue from operations less employee and other expenses, EXCLUDING other income (Rs952 crore FY2026: interest, dividends, surcharge); the matching assets (JV stakes, PG InvIT and other investments, mutual funds, net held-for-sale) are in the equity bridge at book. Regulatory deferral account balances (Rs6,496 crore asset) roughly offset the deferred tax liability (Rs6,260 crore) and are left out of the bridge. FY2026 EBITDA margin of 81.3% was depressed by FX losses in other expenses; H1 FY2027 ran at 82.6%. Cash tax is the MAT rate (current tax 17.2% of PBT in H1 FY2027) ramping to the 25% regime by FY2036. Base revenue and FCF are FY2026 (March 2026) actuals while net debt is the September 2026 balance sheet; H1 FY2027 FCF was about -Rs240 crore, so the overlap is immaterial. SBC-zero market: band_position is not meaningful (house = street). Finance-lease/service-concession TBCB assets return principal through investing cash flow ('financial lease receipts'), which this EBITDA-based build does not capture -- a small conservative omission today that grows as more TBCB assets are capitalised that way.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: driver-built: 10-year base revenue CAGR from the capitalisation schedule (below equity_5yr_cagr of 7.5%)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR (7.5%) is more than double revenue 5yr CAGR (3.3%) and revenue has been flat for three years (FY2023 Rs45,581 crore -> FY2026 Rs46,733 crore): book value compounds through retention while tariffs on the legacy asset base decay. Equity CAGR is therefore not used as the growth rate; revenue is built from capitalisation instead.
historical_growth.notes: No SBC, so owner FCF equals reported FCF (OCF less capex; Indian cash flow statements put finance costs in financing, so this is close to unlevered). FCF fell from Rs31,102 crore (FY2023) to Rs3,651 crore (FY2026) because capex rose from Rs6,903 crore to Rs37,279 crore, not because operating cash flow weakened (OCF Rs38,005 crore -> Rs40,931 crore). FCF CAGRs are a capex-cycle artefact and carry no signal.

base.capex_note: Rs bn: 385, 430, 450, 450, 430, 400, 360, 320, 285, 255. FY2027 is the midpoint of the Rs37,000-40,000 crore guidance (H1 cash capex Rs18,913 crore). FY2027-32 sums to ~Rs2.55 lakh crore: the Rs2.20 lakh crore order book plus about half the Rs67,200 crore bidding pipeline. After FY2032 (the end of the National Electricity Plan window) capex glides to ~32% of revenue, the level that funds ~4% growth at the assumed tariff yield.
base.growth_rationale: Capitalisation Rs bn 275 (guidance 250-300), 350, 420, 450, 450, 430, 390, 350, 310, 275. Incremental revenue = 12.5% first-year tariff yield on capitalisation (half-year lag) less legacy tariff decay of ~Rs17bn/yr through FY2032, fading to Rs6bn by FY2036. Calibration: Rs28,206 crore capitalised in FY2026 lifted H1 FY2027 revenue only 2.8% YoY, which fixes yield-less-decay; H1 FY2027 TBCB wins of Rs8,100 crore annual tariff against a ~Rs55-60,000 crore rise in works in hand indicate ~13-14% on NCT cost.
base.narrative: Order book executed on schedule at current TBCB economics; legacy RAB tariffs keep decaying; capex normalises after FY2032.

bull.capex_note: Rs bn: 400, 460, 500, 500, 490, 460, 430, 390, 340, 300 -- the full pipeline is won and Green Energy Corridor III adds to it.
bull.growth_rationale: Capitalisation Rs bn 300, 380, 460, 500, 500, 480, 450, 420, 380, 330 at a 14% tariff yield (the H1 FY2027 win economics hold), legacy decay ~Rs13bn/yr fading to Rs5bn. EBITDA margin returns to the FY2025 level (85%) as high-margin TBCB annuities grow in the mix.
bull.narrative: Incumbency and AAA funding keep win economics intact; execution runs ahead of the right-of-way constraint.

bear.capex_note: Rs bn: 360, 370, 370, 350, 330, 300, 280, 260, 240, 225 -- lower win rate and right-of-way slippage hold spend below guidance.
bear.growth_rationale: Capitalisation Rs bn 250, 300, 340, 360, 350, 330, 300, 280, 260, 240 at an 11% tariff yield (bid IRRs compressed by Adani Energy Solutions, Resonia, Sterlite; some cost overruns disallowed by CERC), legacy decay ~Rs18bn/yr. EBITDA margin stays near the FY2026 level.
bear.narrative: Competition and regulatory disallowance turn the capex ramp into low-return growth; capitalisation lags spend.

scenario_narratives.base: The Rs2.20 lakh crore order book (89% TBCB) and about half the bidding pipeline are built through FY2032 at capex of Rs38-45,000 crore a year, capitalised with the usual lag, and earn a 12.5% first-year tariff yield. Against that, the legacy cost-plus asset base keeps losing roughly Rs1,700 crore of tariff a year as normative loans amortise and the FY2015-20 capitalisation wave passes year 12 of the CERC depreciation schedule -- the reason revenue has been flat since FY2023 despite rising capitalisation. Revenue growth therefore peaks near 7% in FY2030-31, not the double digits a capex-to-revenue shortcut would give. Competitively bid projects are priced close to the cost of capital, so growth adds little value per rupee invested; the equity is worth the in-place regulated assets plus work-in-progress at about cost. Free cash flow is negative through FY2030 and debt keeps rising. After FY2032 capex glides to a steady state.
scenario_narratives.bull: POWERGRID keeps its ~47% cumulative TBCB tariff share without giving up price: new projects earn ~14% on cost (the H1 FY2027 win economics), the whole pipeline plus Green Energy Corridor Phase III work is won, right-of-way delays stay contained and capitalisation reaches Rs50,000 crore a year. Margins recover to 85% as flat-tariff TBCB annuities outweigh the decaying legacy book, and the AAA funding advantage over private bidders persists. Revenue roughly doubles in ten years.
scenario_narratives.bear: Adani Energy Solutions, Resonia and Sterlite compress bid IRRs so new assets earn ~11% on cost; CERC disallows part of cost overruns under the 2024-29 regulations; land and forest clearances keep capitalisation running behind spend, so interest during construction accumulates on a balance sheet already at 1.4x debt:equity. Legacy tariff decay continues at full pace. The capex programme becomes low-return growth funded by debt and revenue grows only 3-4% a year. The equity ends up worth roughly book value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: every rupee of revenue depends on a single regulator (CERC) and a single policy owner (the 51.34% government shareholder), and the competitive pressure on bid returns is already visible. Base 50%: it is calibrated to the observed H1 FY2027 revenue response and to guided capex and capitalisation. Bull cut from 35% to 25%: it needs win economics, win rate, execution pace and margins all to hold at once while competition is intensifying.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated grid is worth its in-place assets plus whatever new investment earns above the cost of capital. POWERGRID's legacy cost-plus book earns well above that cost but is amortising; its growth is now won in auctions that price returns close to it. The DCF therefore values the business at roughly 1.4x book in the base case, not the 2.2x the market pays. The gap to the market price is a discount-rate and terminal-multiple gap: at an 8.5% INR WACC (cost of equity ~11.4%) and a terminal value capped at 20x FCF the shares are worth well under the price even in the bull case. The base case reaches the price only if the 70:30 regulatory debt structure is treated as the capital structure (WACC ~7.5-7.7%) and the terminal value is left uncapped. Free cash flow is negative until about FY2031, so over 85% of enterprise value is terminal value and the equity is a geared residual: enterprise value moves about 1% for every 3% move in value per share. A 15% hurdle is not available from a regulated 8-9% asset at anything near the current price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Discount rate: the equity is a geared residual (net debt is about half of enterprise value). Base value per share falls ~9% from 8.5% to 9.0% WACC and ~45% by 10%; it rises ~19% at 7.5%, where the 20x terminal cap limits the gain
Tariff yield on new capitalisation (11% bear / 12.5% base / 14% bull) and the pace of legacy tariff decay are estimated from disclosed aggregates, not project-level tariff orders
Terminal value is capped at 20x FCF and exceeds 85% of enterprise value; the terminal year assumes capex has fallen to ~32% of revenue after FY2032
Upside not modelled: principal recovery on finance-lease/service-concession TBCB assets, tax pass-through on cost-plus assets as the cash tax rate rises, and incentive income
Downside not modelled: an equity raise or forced higher dividend from the government shareholder while debt:equity is rising
